controlcompR: Control Systems, Optimal Control, and Model Predictive Control in R

Source: R/utils.R
controlcompR-package.Rd

A unified framework for modeling, analyzing, designing and simulating linear and nonlinear control systems. It provides validated continuous-time and discrete-time state-space and transfer-function models, exact zero-order-hold, first-order-hold and Tustin discretization, time and frequency responses, stability, controllability and observability analysis with scale-aware tolerances, Schur-based Lyapunov solvers, Riccati solvers based on ordered generalized Schur decompositions of extended pencils, linear quadratic regulators, pole placement, PID controllers with derivative filtering, anti-windup and bumpless transfer, Luenberger observers, Kalman filters and smoothers, LQG controllers, gain, phase and disk margins, H2 and H-infinity norms, H2 and (experimental, certified) H-infinity synthesis, balanced truncation, constrained linear model predictive control solved with 'OSQP' (input, rate, state and output constraints, soft constraints, offset-free tracking), moving horizon estimation, subspace and ARX system identification, and nonlinear simulation, linearization, extended and unscented Kalman filters and nonlinear model predictive control. The design is inspired by 'python-control' https://python-control.org and 'ControlSystems.jl' https://github.com/JuliaControl/ControlSystems.jl; no Python or Julia is required.
